description:
Reproject a road network layer to a metric CRS and calculate road lengths, then export the result as a CSV.

1. Open QGIS (it should already be running).
2. Add the line layer from /home/ga/GIS_Data/sample_lines.geojson using Layer > Add Layer > Add Vector Layer.
3. The layer is in WGS84 (EPSG:4326) which uses degrees, not meters. Reproject it to EPSG:32610 (WGS 84 / UTM zone 10N, which covers the San Francisco Bay Area): right-click the layer > Export > Save Features As. Set the CRS to EPSG:32610, save as GeoJSON to /home/ga/GIS_Data/exports/roads_utm.geojson. Add the saved layer to the map.
4. Open the attribute table of the reprojected layer (right-click > Open Attribute Table).
5. Use the Field Calculator (pencil icon to toggle editing, then the abacus icon): create a new field called 'length_km' of type Decimal (double), with the expression $length / 1000 to compute each road's length in kilometers. Click OK.
6. Save the edits (click the pencil icon again to stop editing, confirm save).
7. Export the final result as CSV: right-click the layer > Export > Save Features As. Choose CSV format. Save to /home/ga/GIS_Data/exports/road_measurements.csv. Make sure 'Add saved file to map' is unchecked or just close the dialog after saving.
